title: Freeze the Vercel-managed Convex URL for server routes

target.candidate_state: published first implementation plus an independently reviewed direct-access correction awaiting hosted PR verification

north_star: Ensure the estimate server route always calls the Convex deployment selected by the Vercel build and never a stale runtime environment URL.

evidence.hosted_root_cause: confirmed — Vercel deployed and seeded cool-lynx-973, but the first hosted POST returned temporarily_unavailable while a stale branch runtime NEXT_PUBLIC_CONVEX_URL remained configured
evidence.first_pr_e2e: failed safely — the first PR #34 deployment returned 503 because a generic environment-object indirection prevented Next.js from inlining CONVEX_DEPLOYMENT_URL
evidence.implementation: pass locally — next.config freezes Convex's build-injected URL as CONVEX_DEPLOYMENT_URL and the helper now defaults its string parameter directly from process.env.CONVEX_DEPLOYMENT_URL so Next.js can inline it
evidence.fail_closed: pass — missing, placeholder, or invalid build URL throws CONVEX_NOT_CONFIGURED; there is no fallback to NEXT_PUBLIC_CONVEX_URL
evidence.focused_tests: pass — 28 tests cover direct build access, managed URL use, fail-closed behavior, Next config mapping, lead intake, and environment schema
evidence.static_checks: pass — lint, tsc --noEmit, and git diff --check passed
evidence.dependency_audit: pass — npm audit reported zero vulnerabilities
evidence.independent_review: pass — evaluator confirmed direct process.env access is the correct Next.js inlining boundary, stale runtime fallback remains excluded, and Production isolation is preserved

residual_risk: The corrected dev deployment must return accepted=true for a hosted synthetic lead before stale Preview URL variables are deleted.
